claim: A navigation system that combines global waypoint selection from points of interest with a deep reinforcement learning-based local navigation policy achieves performance close to the optimal solution obtained by a path planner that has full knowledge of the environment, when operating in unknown environments without prior map information.
falsifier: The claim can be tested by implementing a navigation system with global waypoint selection (e.g., IDLE) and a DRL local policy (e.g., TD3), deploying it in unknown environments without prior maps, and comparing its performance (e.g., mapped area, goals reached, path length) to that of a path planner with full environmental knowledge under the same conditions.

conditions: unknown environment without prior map or human control
continuous action space using TD3 actor-critic
waypoints selected via Information-based Distance Limited Exploration (IDLE) evaluation
Gaussian noise added to sensor and action values during training
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the reported system, simulation and real-world experimental conditions, and performance metrics; transfer beyond these settings is unestablished.

title: Global waypoint selection–navigation performance close principle

claim: Providing full experiment history as shared memory to the data analysis agent improves consistency in feature selection and reduces repeated proposal of low-value features in a multi-agent scientific discovery system.
falsifier: In a multi-agent scientific discovery system, compare feature selection consistency when the data analysis agent has access to full experiment history versus only current iteration records, measuring the frequency of repeated low-value feature proposals.

conditions: when the data analysis agent is restricted to only the current iteration records, consistency decreases and repeated low-value features are proposed
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the reported system, task (grapevine red blotch disease), and experimental conditions; transfer beyond them is unestablished.

title: Full experiment history as for consistency in feature selection

claim: The mapping f(A,B)=((1-|B|)A, BA) is injective on the domain A≠0, B∈(-1,1)\{0}.
falsifier: For any two distinct inputs (A,B) and (a,b) in the domain, verify that f(A,B)≠f(a,b).
title: The mapping f defined–Injectivity of f theorem
